title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
one_line: Across 97 published return predictors, returns were ~26% lower out of sample before publication and ~58% lower after publication; about 32% of the decline is due to publication itself, peaking 3-4 years later.

findings.statement: ~32% decline attributable to publication; largest 3-4 years after.
Bigger decay for stronger in-sample results and price/volume-only signals.

why.pattern: Market adaptation: publication attracts arbitrage capital.

reported_results.headline: Expect less than half of published returns.

tradable_edge: A rule for every spec: assume about half of the paper's reported edge, less after costs; price/volume signals decay most.
angles: Haircut published numbers by ~50% when setting expectations
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
